title: Skills: teaching agents the checks they keep forgetting
summary: Drake turns repeated agent mistakes into skills: a SKILL.md with name and description frontmatter (the description says when to load it) and a body of checks pinned to a source commit with verified examples. He ships them in the public omega-harness repo and installs them as symlinks, so a git pull updates every agent while a copy goes stale. I can run a frontmatter checker on his real skills and on three broken ones.
goal: Write skills that load at the right moment and install them so a pull keeps every agent current.
key_steps: Make frontmatter name equal the directory name
Write a description that says when to use the skill
Pin every claim in the body to a source commit and rerun its examples
Install by symlinking the clone's skill directories, not by copying
Check the frontmatter with a negative control that must fail

example.code:
#!/bin/sh
# check-skill.sh SKILL_DIR: check the Agent Skills frontmatter of SKILL_DIR/SKILL.md.
# Rules: line 1 is ---, a closing --- follows, name equals the directory name, and description
# is present and says when to use the skill (contains "Use "). Exit 0 PASS, 1 FAIL, 2 usage.
dir=${1:?usage: check-skill.sh SKILL_DIR}
skill=$(basename "$dir")
f=$dir/SKILL.md
fail() { printf 'FAIL %s: %s\n' "$skill" "$1"; exit 1; }
[ -f "$f" ] || fail 'no SKILL.md'
[ "$(sed -n 1p "$f")" = '---' ] || fail 'line 1 is not ---'
end=$(awk 'NR > 1 && $0 == "---" { print NR; exit }' "$f")
[ -n "$end" ] || fail 'frontmatter is never closed'
front=$(sed -n "2,$((end - 1))p" "$f")
name=$(printf '%s\n' "$front" | sed -n 's/^name: *//p')
desc=$(printf '%s\n' "$front" | sed -n 's/^description: *//p')
[ -n "$name" ] || fail 'no name'
[ "$name" = "$skill" ] || fail "name '$name' differs from directory '$skill'"
[ -n "$desc" ] || fail 'no description'
printf '%s\n' "$desc" | grep -q 'Use ' || fail 'description never says when to use it'
printf 'PASS %s: name ok, description %s bytes, body %s lines\n' "$skill" "$(printf '%s' "$desc" | wc -c | tr -d ' ')" "$(($(wc -l < "$f") - end))"

common_mistake: A description that says what the skill is instead of when to use it, so it never loads; or a copied install that silently goes stale. Fix: say 'Use when/before ...' in the description and install by symlink, then pull.
evidence_note: The example ran on a Linux AArch64 host (no GPU) and its output is recorded byte for byte with a negative control. Rests on the recorded run: all six omega-harness skills pass the frontmatter check at commit 9ab649cd, three malformed skills fail, and a symlinked install follows a pull while a copy does not. NOT done: whether skills change agent behavior is unmeasured (the SI index lists omega-harness as IMPLEMENTED with no CI).
